title: Persian and English without a model: one normalisation, Persian tables, quotes in the person's script
request: Complete the Home plan package by package; H3 makes Home's no-model path read Persian as well as English, since the owner works in Persian and the rules were English regular expressions.
spec: Package H3 of Phase H in docs/guides/AGENTIC_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md: draft/lang.py with normalisation (Arabic yeh and kaf, digits for matching only, ZWNJ, diacritics) and pattern tables per language for intent, outcome windows, prediction moments, build and simulate words; plan.extract, the intent rules and the chat's word checks use it; quotes keep the person's original text; Arabic later. Done when: on H1 dev with no model, Persian requests reach at least the same track accuracy as English ones.
plan: Write a normalisation that returns an index back into the original text, so a match on the folded text is quoted from what the person wrote.
Write the Persian intent table at the same weights as the English one, from the H1 dev requests and ordinary Persian, never the sealed set.
Run both tables on the normalised text in the intent rules; grow quotes through a ZWNJ, which is inside a Persian word.
Add Persian outcome-with-window and set-apart moment rules to plan.extract, after the English ones, so English is unchanged.
Make the quote rule fold both sides, and the chat's build and simulate checks read both languages.
Test each pattern in several spellings, quotes in the original script, English unchanged; measure H1 dev and compare every English case with HOME-002.

decisions.decision: Normalise with an index map instead of matching the raw text.
decisions.why: Persian is written with a ZWNJ or a space, Arabic or Persian yeh and kaf, and Persian or Western digits; one folded form lets one pattern match them all, and the map keeps the quote in the person's own spelling.

decisions.decision: Persian plan rules run only when the English rules find nothing.
decisions.why: English extraction must stay exactly as it was; a mixed sentence with an English outcome keeps it.

decisions.decision: "بساز" alone is not a build word.
decisions.why: It is also "make me a pivot"; the build words name the solution, the project or the model.
H3 is about understanding; replying in Persian needs every message of Home in Persian, which is a package of its own.

change: New dclab_rnd/draft/lang.py (normalize, fold, span, finditer, search, has, script; INTENT_FA, TARGET_FA, MOMENTS_FA, BUILD, SIMULATE). intent.py: both tables on the normalised text, quotes mapped back, ZWNJ inside words. plan.py: _norm folds with lang, extract falls back to the Persian rules. chat.py: BUILD_WORDS and SIMULATE_WORDS read both languages. tests/test_home_lang.py (15 tests). HOME-003_dev.

findings.scenario: In 'چرا مشتری‌ها می‌روند' the folded text holds 'می روند', and the analysis signal for a trend ('روند') matched inside the verb.
findings.cause: The ZWNJ becomes a space, so the verb's stem stands as a word of its own.
findings.fix: The trend signal never matches after 'می' or 'نمی'.

findings.defect: The Persian difference signal matched inside ordinary words.
findings.scenario: '…با پلن‌های متفاوت لغو می‌کنند' (customers on different plans will cancel) and 'فرقی نمی‌کند چه الگوریتمی…' (it doesn't matter which algorithm) were read as advice.
findings.cause: 'فرق|تفاوت' at weight 4 with no word boundary.
findings.fix: Weight 3, and only 'فرق/تفاوت بین…', '… X با/و Y' or 'چه فرقی دارد'.

findings.defect: Persian signals had no word boundaries.
findings.scenario: 'مجموع' matched 'مجموعه' (dataset) and 'رصد' matched 'درصد' (percent), so 'بر اساس این مجموعه داده، کدام مشتری‌ها لغو می‌کنند؟' left the prediction path.
findings.fix: Every Persian pattern is wrapped in Persian-letter boundaries (letters only: '،' and '؟' sit in the same Unicode block); 'چند درصد' is an analysis share signal; 'ماه بعد از' is not a future period.

findings.scenario: 'کدام مشتری‌ها برای پیشنهاد تخفیف مناسب است؟' (which customers suit a discount?) was read as advice.
findings.cause: The advice signals did not require a question about the method.
findings.fix: 'آیا … مناسب است' or 'مناسب است که'; 'چیست' only at the end of a question; 'چه معیاری/روشی' only with 'بهتر/مناسب/استفاده'.

findings.defect: Persian predictions in the future tense or with 'مدلی' were missed.
findings.scenario: 'مشتری جدید چقدر خرید خواهد کرد؟' was read as analysis; 'مدلی بساز که هر هفته پیش‌بینی کند…' was asked.
findings.cause: No future-tense signal; the model signal needed 'مدل' followed by a space.

findings.scenario: A model's '۳۰ روز آینده' passed against the person's 'ظرف 30 روز آینده', and one word with a ZWNJ counted as two, so a quote that was not the person's text could be stored.
findings.cause: plan._norm was switched to the full fold.
findings.fix: The quote rule is back to the person's exact words (case and spaces only); the rules still read through the fold and quote the original.

findings.scenario: 'قبل از اینکه شروع کنیم، ستون مبلغ نهایی بعد از رزرو پر می‌شود' (a leakage note) showed the summary instead of being recorded.
findings.fix: Only a message that is itself 'let's start' (بیا/خب/پس شروع کنیم).

findings.defect: Normalising turned a line break into a space and changed an English reading.
findings.scenario: 'How many orders did we have last month?\nDo we need a model for that?' lost its how_much signal.
findings.cause: The how_much lookahead stops at a line end, which the fold removed.
findings.fix: A line break stays a line break in the normalised text.

findings.defect: The index map shifted after a character that lowers to two.
findings.scenario: Text with 'İ' moved every later quote by one character.
findings.cause: One index entry was kept for two output characters.
findings.fix: One index entry per output character.

findings.defect: Persian plan rules missed common forms.
findings.scenario: 'تخمین بزن چند سفارش در هفته آینده ثبت می‌شود' gave no outcome; '…، دو روز قبل از ورود' gave no moment; a Persian quote could never support a model's value.
findings.cause: No 'بزن' verb, no number words, and supports() read only Latin letters.
findings.fix: Added both forms; supports() compares Unicode word stems.

measurements.name: Home on the H1 dev requests, rules alone, after H3 (HOME-003)
measurements.gate: home_gate_v1: track accuracy with the model at least 0.85 and with the rules alone at least 0.70; no new wrong field, bad quote, uncited number, identifier shown or unconfirmed row drop; median questions at most 3; every trap passes
measurements.result: Track accuracy 1.0 (36/36): English 1.0, Persian 1.0, mixed 1.0 (Persian was 0.125 in HOME-002). Every English case unchanged against HOME-002. Traps 4/6 (persian_no_model now passes). Quotes, uncited numbers and rows shown 0. Fields lost to I'm not sure: 3 (a Persian outcome is now understood, then lost the same way as the English ones; H4 fixes it). The dev split holds 8 Persian and 4 mixed requests; the reviewer's own ordinary Persian sentences were 12, 6 of them misread before the fixes and none after.
measurements.against_gate: rules_track_accuracy 1.0 against at least 0.70: met; quote_invalid 0 and uncited 0 against 0: met; median questions 0 against at most 3: met; traps 4 of 6 against all: not met; the gate is read with the model, which has not run.
limits: The Persian and English tables were written by the author of the sealed set, from the dev requests; the sealed run (H12) is the honest test.
Eight Persian and four mixed dev requests are few; ordinary Persian sentences in tests/test_home_lang.py add twelve more.

The first review found six of twelve ordinary Persian sentences of its own misread; after the fixes all of them, and the dev requests, read right, which shows how far twelve dev requests are from coverage.

outcome: With no model, a Persian request now gets its kind of help, its outcome and window, and its moment when it is set apart, quoted in the person's own spelling; English reads exactly as before.
lessons: Fold once, quote from the original: an index map from the normalised text back to the person's text keeps every rule simple and every quote honest.
A reviewer's own ordinary sentences are the honest test of hand-written rules: the dev set had been met while half of ordinary Persian was still misread.
risks: Persian verbs and stems become separate words after folding a ZWNJ, so a short signal can match inside a verb; every short Persian signal needs a test against ordinary verbs.
